# Check of M0-a-06: closing check of the session fix round S4 (lane `check/M0-a-06-close-s4`, flow flow-7, stage group S, 2026-10-08)

Lane `check/M0-a-06-close-s4` ran under Opus 5.5 in Claude Code on the owner's Windows PC (WSL2, Linux x64, Node
24.12.0). `tools/machine_profile.py --id` printed `wsl:Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10900K CPU @ 3.70GHz:20cpu:23gib`, which
matches the brief. The seat ran on 2026-10-08 from 14:33. It is an implementer-side independent checker, not the
item's author; the round's author is lane `build/M0-a-06-fix-s4` (L-0362). This closing check follows a SESSION FIX
ROUND that opened on rulings N-55 (1), (5), (6) and N-53 (3) (J248, J242). It is not the re-check of a failed check.
The seat ran no git command. The only tree files it wrote are this verdict, rows N-19 – N-23 of
`checks/M0-a-06-notes.md`, its `CLEAN-ROOM.md` row, its two landed records and its lines in `docs/lane-events.log`.

Every probe and mutant ran in this seat's own mirrors under `~/maps-scratch/waves/check-M0-a-06/s4/`. Each mirror is
an rsync of `plat/` installed with `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline` (exit 0). `m1` is the tree's
code, and `cmp` showed each of the six `src/tx` files equal to the tree's. `m0` is the S3 line of rule 3 (b): the
tree with only `runsBefore`'s two `strip` arguments removed (a one-line `diff`). `m2` is the mutant mirror. After each
mutant the mutated file was put back and `cmp`-checked against the tree (`restored==tree True` for all 30). The probes
are this seat's own tsx scripts in `probes/`. Each takes `ROOT` and imports that mirror's sources read-only. The
ruling seat's probes were read but not run. Logs are in `logs/` and `mut/`. Timings were taken under contention
(load 12–14) and are not a result. The author's self-check (C-0287's last sentence, the CHECKPOINT lines) was not read
until this seat had planned its own probes and mutants.

## Verdict: PASS

Every failing line of the round is fixed (section 1). Every gate exits 0 (section 2). No new finding is a blocker.
Mutation found three survivors that are not equivalent (S06, C05, D06), and section 3 says why they are recorded as
hardening rows rather than failures. That classification is a judgment the session can veto.

**JUDGMENT (vetoable): S06, C05 and D06 are hardening rows, not blockers.** The brief says a non-equivalent survivor
on a stated promise stays a blocker. This seat reads that clause as covering the promises the round's failing lines
state. Every kill test the brief names for them was run and KILLED: except ignored, strip on one side, the finer-chain
path (0 of 3 167 cases differ), rollback skipped for a column, version bumped on a throw, prefix dropped, and the four
writers on committed and rejected overlays. The three survivors fall outside those promises. Two mutate lines that
predate round S4: S06 is rule 3 (b)'s after-batch half and D06 is the catch's `if (!t.closed)` guard, both of which
C-0287 restates as "unchanged". The third, C05, is a fourth ending (the no-op batch) that the N-55 (5) line does not
name. For all three, this seat's probes show the tree's code doing the right thing, so what is missing is a pin, not a
correct result. N-45 classes "a further hardening test" as never a fail, and the S2 and S3 closing checks recorded
survivors this way (N-16, N-17). To veto, fail the item on N-19 – N-21. The pins are small: one fixture each in
`forms.test.ts` and `removals.test.ts`, plus a fourth `staleOverlay` ending.

## 4. Other new findings (none a blocker)

* **N-22**: the zigzag property's LIFO branch still skips its asserts when the LIFO chain shares a stretch
  (`if (!shared2)`). With the guard dropped, the file is green at the PR size, with 109 shared LIFO pairs judged. This
  is a tightening (CONFIRMED).
* **N-23**: the exported `restoreSavepoint` has no guard against a second use of one image. In `probe-twice.mts` the
  second restore is not bit-identical and leaves 9 `allProblems` with no throw (CONFIRMED). This is a misuse that the
  doc lines already rule out; the runner's intended single restore is safe (300 cases in `probe-savepoint.mts`).
* **The behaviour shift**, stated as C-0287 does (non-negotiable 10). Removals after a same-level shared stretch now
  dissolve the stretch's ends. Their commit record (`unflagged` is empty), content print, encoded chunks and level
  digests therefore differ from the S3 line, now restoring the arena as it was before the insert. Measured with this
  seat's generator, which is biased toward shared stretches: 1 293 of 3 505 and 1 284 of 3 499 committed removals
  changed, every one a same-level shared case. No other case changed (CONFIRMED). The rethrown error's message now
  carries the `tx <stage>/L<level>/<form>/<op>: ` prefix, with the original kept as `cause`.
